--- title: "One number, three answers: KPI governance at Vallora Logística" description: "Three departments, three absenteeism rates for the same month. How 40 KPIs became 14, each with a definition sheet, an owner and a change rule." image: img/capa.png image-alt: "Case cover: one number, three answers, KPI governance at Vallora Logística, with the chart of the three absenteeism rates" categories: [KPI governance, KPIs, Management, R] # Frente de serviço, para o filtro de Projetos: paineis, pesquisas e/ou indicadores. frente: [indicadores] traducao: indicadores # Tapping a chart opens it full screen (on phones the charts are small). lightbox: true format: html: code-fold: true code-summary: "Show the R code" execute: warning: false message: false knitr: opts_chunk: dev: ragg_png dev.args: { bg: transparent } fig.align: center --- ::: aviso-dados **Fictional case.** Vallora Logística S.A., its departments, people and KPIs do not exist. The three absenteeism rates were calculated from the fictional dataset of the [Absenteeism Radar](../absenteeism-radar/index.qmd); the inventory, the definition sheets and the rules were written for this case. The method is real. [Download the three monthly rates (CSV)](../../../projetos/governanca-indicadores/dados/taxa_tres_definicoes.csv){download="taxa_tres_definicoes.csv"} · [Download the KPI inventory (CSV)](../../../projetos/governanca-indicadores/dados/inventario.csv){download="inventario.csv"} ::: [The CSV files and the comments in the R code are in Portuguese, the case's original language.]{.nota-idioma} ## The story At the July 2025 results meeting, Vallora heard three absenteeism rates for June. HR showed 4.38%, Operations 3.54% and Finance 2.15%, and the meeting spent half an hour arguing about which one was right. ::: so-computador ::: {.cell layout-align="center" lightbox='{"group":"computador"}'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Absenteeism rate calculated each department's way, from January 2024 to December 2025. The vertical line marks June 2025, the month discussed at the July meeting.](index_files/figure-html/taxas-1.png){fig-align='center' fig-alt='Three monthly lines. HR, in blue, stays above Operations almost all the time; Finance runs well below both. In June 2025, marked by the July meeting line, the three are far apart.' width=864} ::: ::: ::: ::: so-celular ::: {.cell layout-align="center" lightbox='{"group":"celular"}'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Absenteeism rate calculated each department's way, from January 2024 to December 2025. The vertical line marks June 2025, the month discussed at the July meeting.](index_files/figure-html/taxas-celular-1.png){fig-align='center' fig-alt='Three monthly lines. HR, in blue, stays above Operations almost all the time; Finance runs well below both. In June 2025, marked by the July meeting line, the three are far apart.' width=432} ::: ::: ::: None of them was wrong. Each department calculated what it needed for its own work and gave the result the same name. The problem was not arithmetic, it was governance: nobody had written down what "absenteeism rate" meant at the company, or who got to decide. The scene repeated itself over the following months, and in December leadership asked for an inventory of every KPI that circulated in the monthly presentations. Forty turned up, from six departments, and only 13 were well defined. The work took five weeks, in four stages: 1. Interviews with the people who produce the numbers and the people who use them, in all six departments. 2. Inventory and diagnosis of each KPI. 3. Definition sheets for the KPIs that go to leadership. 4. Governance rules: who proposes, who approves, how a change is recorded. ## The divergence: three calculations, one name The three rates come from the same data and answer different questions. The decision was to keep all three, each with its own name, and reserve "Absenteeism rate" for HR's definition, which is the same as the Radar's. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{=html}

``` ::: - **Operations.** Operations counts the whole day even when the absence is a late arrival, which pushes the rate up, but takes anyone absent for more than 15 days off the schedule, which pulls it down. On balance, it lands a little below HR. In four of the 24 months (January and February 2024, September and November 2025), the balance flipped: in months with few long-term absences, counting the whole day weighs more, and Operations comes out above HR. - **Finance.** It leaves out unexcused absences and late arrivals that are docked from pay, and whatever INSS pays from day 16 of a leave. That is why it runs well below the other two. In Brazil, the employer pays the first 15 days of sick or injury leave; from day 16 on, the social security agency (INSS) pays. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{.r .cell-code code-summary="Show the R code for the three definitions"} # Tipos da base: 1 atestado médico, 2 consulta ou exame (parcial), 3 acidente # de trabalho, 4 afastamento do INSS, 5 falta injustificada, 6 atraso ou saída # antecipada, 7 licença legal (CLT art. 473), 8 acompanhamento de dependente, # 9 licença maternidade/paternidade (dias já fora da jornada no Radar). # RH: horas de ausência dos tipos que contam no Radar ÷ horas previstas. rh <- ausencias |> filter(considera_taxa == 1) # Operação: dias escalados com qualquer ausência (atraso ou saída antecipada só # acima de 10 minutos) ÷ dias escalados. Quem está afastado há mais de 15 dias # (do 16º dia de um evento longo em diante) sai da escala, no numerador e no # denominador. afastado <- ausencias |> filter(dias_corridos > 15, dia_do_evento > 15) |> distinct(id_funcionario, data) escala <- jornada |> anti_join(afastado, c("id_funcionario", "data")) dias_com_ausencia <- escala |> semi_join(filter(ausencias, id_tipo_ausencia != 6 | horas_ausencia * 60 > 10), c("id_funcionario", "data")) # Financeiro: horas pagas pela empresa ÷ horas previstas. Entram atestados e # acidentes de até 15 dias, consultas, licenças legais e os 15 primeiros dias # dos afastamentos longos por doença ou acidente (tipos 1, 3 e 4), que a empresa # paga por lei. Ficam fora faltas e atrasos (descontados), o que o INSS paga e # o acompanhamento de dependente. pagas <- ausencias |> filter(id_tipo_ausencia == 7 | (id_tipo_ausencia %in% c(1, 2, 3) & dias_corridos <= 15) | (id_tipo_ausencia %in% c(1, 3, 4) & dias_corridos > 15 & dia_do_evento <= 15)) ``` ::: ## Diagnosis: from 40 to 14 Of the 40 KPIs, 14 go to the leadership meeting, 14 stay with the departments and 12 leave the presentations, merged or discontinued. Each KPI was given a status and a destination, using the criteria below. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Status found |Criterion | Count| |:---------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----:| |Well defined |Written formula, single source, an owner, and used in some decision | 13| |Inconsistent |Same name, different calculations across departments or sites | 7| |Duplicate |Different names for the same measure, or one is a slice of the other | 7| |Poorly designed |Volume with no reference point, a slice treated as a KPI, or the wrong incentive | 6| |Unused |Not part of any decision recorded in the minutes in the last six months | 4| |No owner |Nobody answers for the result or the calculation | 3| ::: ::: ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Destination |What it means | Count| |:----------------|:-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----:| |Leadership |Goes to the monthly meeting, with a full definition sheet, a target and an owner | 14| |Department level |The department tracks it with a short definition sheet; it goes to leadership only by exception | 14| |Merged |Becomes part of another KPI or a breakdown of it | 6| |Discontinued |Leaves the presentations; the data remain available | 6| ::: ::: ::: so-computador ::: {.cell layout-align="center" lightbox='{"group":"computador"}'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Where each KPI came from and where it went. The width of each band is the number of KPIs.](index_files/figure-html/fluxo-1.png){fig-align='center' fig-alt='Flow diagram with the six statuses on the left and the four destinations on the right. The bands that reach Leadership, in blue, come mostly from Well defined and Inconsistent.' width=864} ::: ::: ::: ::: so-celular ::: {.cell layout-align="center" lightbox='{"group":"celular"}'} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Where each KPI came from and where it went. The width of each band is the number of KPIs.](index_files/figure-html/fluxo-celular-1.png){fig-align='center' fig-alt='Flow diagram with the six statuses on the left and the four destinations on the right. The bands that reach Leadership, in blue, come mostly from Well defined and Inconsistent.' width=432} ::: ::: ::: To go to leadership, a KPI has to pass three questions: it is tied to a company objective, someone in leadership makes a decision with it, and it moves enough from one month to the next to deserve the meeting. The most instructive case is "Days without accidents". It looks positive, but it rewards not reporting accidents; the Accident frequency rate measures the same thing without that incentive. ## Inventory: the 40 KPIs Only 13 of the 40 KPIs were well defined. The table shows the full inventory, with search and filters by department, status and destination. ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}

The decision belongs to a KPI committee: the financial controller chairs it, the owners of the 14 KPIs take part, and the BI analyst keeps the minutes. It meets once a month, for 30 minutes, only when there are requests in the queue. ### Roles (RACI matrix) R does the work, A approves and answers for it, C is consulted, I is informed. ::: so-computador ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ::: {.cell-output-display} |Activity | KPI owner | BI analyst | Committee | Leadership | |:-----------------------------------------------|:---------:|:----------:|:---------:|:----------:| |Propose a new KPI or a change of definition | R | C | A | I | |Measure the impact of the change | C | R | A | | |Approve or reject the change | C | C | R and A | I | |Update the definition sheet and the version log | I | R | A | | |Calculate and publish every month | C | R and A | | I | |Explain the result and the action plan | R and A | C | | I | |Review the whole set once a year | C | R | A | C | |Discontinue a KPI | C | R | A | I | ::: ::: ::: ::: so-celular ::: {.cell layout-align="center"} ```{=html}

When Operations talks about its rate, it now goes by another name, and the July argument does not happen again. The Absenteeism Radar now uses the official PES-01 definition. ## What this case demonstrates - **Separating the math from the governance.** A divergence is rarely a calculation error; it is almost always the lack of a written definition and of someone who decides. - **Cutting without deleting.** Twenty-six KPIs left the leadership meeting, and no department lost information it needs. - **Definition sheets that answer the questions that start arguments:** what goes in, what stays out, whether higher is better, when the number closes. - **Changes on record**, so that today's number stays comparable with last year's. - **A bridge to BI.** The definition sheets become the DAX measures and the dashboard's data dictionary, and the dashboard stops hiding rules. ::: cta-final ## Does your company argue about which number is right before discussing what to do about it?
